title: Dot product against the zero vector
statement: Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and a length $n \ge 0$, and let $s \in (\bbz/k\bbz)^n$. Writing $0$ for the zero vector of $(\bbz/k\bbz)^n$, the dot product of $s$ with $0$ equals $0$ in $\bbz/k\bbz$; that is, $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} s_i \cdot 0 = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: k is a positive modulus (NeZero k)
s is a vector in (Z/kZ)^n of length n
